audits.title: 858 Post Operative Opioid Prescribing in Patients Undergoing Primary Elective Total Hip Replacement (THR): A Closed-Loop Clinical Audit
audits.standard: NICE NG180 postoperative analgesia recommendations
audits.setting: University College London Hospital, elective primary THR patients aged 60+

cycle1.result: Baseline rates of regular oral opioid prescribing on D0 and time to first oral opioid (figures not given).

audits.intervention: Printed NICE NG180 posters and face-to-face education on postoperative analgesia.

cycle2.result: 30% increase in purely regular oral opioid prescriptions on D0; 10% increase in first oral opioid within 2 hours for those on regular opioids.

audits.other_findings: 2–8 hour and >8 hour timings stayed similar; an electronic prescription order set is proposed.
audits.citation: Moosavi H, Rowe C, Sakariya D, Raja H, Alsawada O, Solanzo A, et al.. 858 Post Operative Opioid Prescribing in Patients Undergoing Primary Elective Total Hip Replacement (THR): A Closed-Loop Clinical Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae163.275.

audits.title: 501 Post-Operative Pain Management in Elective Arthroplasties – Results of a Closed Loop Audit
audits.standard: Hospital perioperative arthroplasty protocol: regular opioids plus regular non-opioid analgesics plus PRN analgesia (score 3)
audits.setting: Orthopaedic department, Royal Surrey County Hospital, Guildford (elective hip and knee arthroplasty)

cycle1.result: 34% achieved protocol-standard analgesia (score 3).

audits.intervention: Elective arthroplasty protocol powerplan implemented in the Surrey Safe Care electronic patient record.

cycle2.result: 61% achieved score 3; 87% of those adherent used the powerplan.

audits.other_findings: A subset of patients still did not receive recommended analgesia; 20 knee and 31 hip arthroplasties in cycle 2.
audits.citation: Dinesh A, Panselinas I, Zafar R, Luck J, Nutt J. 501 Post-Operative Pain Management in Elective Arthroplasties – Results of a Closed Loop Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf128.689.

audits.standard: Local 1994 practice guideline: ketoprofen 50 mg every six hours after surgery with at least moderate expected pain
audits.setting: Hôpital Antoine-Béclère, Clamart

cycle1.result: Ketoprofen not prescribed to 112 (63%), because of minor expected pain (n = 55) or contraindications; used despite contraindication in 11%; nurses omitted at least one dose in 18%.

audits.other_findings: Prescribing despite contraindication was guided by risk/benefit analysis.

audits.title: Postoperative analgesia for Enhanced recovery in Joint replacement: Audit of a new electronic prescribing order set.
audits.standard: Local enhanced recovery multimodal postoperative analgesia protocol for elective hip and knee replacement
audits.setting: Whittington Hospital, London; elective hip and knee arthroplasty in an enhanced recovery programme

cycle1.period: One week at the beginning of July 2014
cycle1.result: 0/27 patients received all medications according to the protocol

audits.intervention: Electronic prescribing order set (JAC) for the analgesia protocol introduced in August 2014; results presented, re-education of rotating junior staff and protocol added to induction documentation

cycle2.result: Total compliance 58%; gabapentin 96%, modified-release morphine 96%, weak opioid 100%, conversion to PRN analgesia 100%, ibuprofen 58%

audits.other_findings: Intermediate cycle in October 2014 (n=26) showed compliance of 34.6% (p<0.001); ibuprofen prescribing stayed poor, with 9/26 omitted without documented contraindication.
audits.citation: Wright J, Cullinger B, Bacarese-Hamilton I. Postoperative analgesia for Enhanced recovery in Joint replacement: Audit of a new electronic prescribing order set. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2015;4(1):u209187.w3753. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u209187.w3753. PMID: 26734429.

audits.title: 421 Closed loop analgesia audit, a Single Centre Experience in Raigmore Hospital, Inverness, Scotland
audits.standard: WHO analgesic ladder, with reasons documented when not followed
audits.setting: Surgical patients, Raigmore Hospital, Inverness

cycle1.result: 83.3% prescribed analgesia following the ladder; of the rest, only 50% had reasons documented.

audits.intervention: Presentation at audit meeting, educational sessions, information leaflets and email reminders.

cycle2.result: Ladder compliance 50.9%; documentation of reasons 56%.

audits.other_findings: 103 patients across both cycles. Authors judged the deviations from the ladder clinically justified.
audits.citation: Chan J. 421 Closed loop analgesia audit, a Single Centre Experience in Raigmore Hospital, Inverness, Scotland. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.051.

audits.title: 75 Audit of Pain Control in Surgical Inpatients
audits.standard: WHO analgesic ladder and NICE 147 guideline
audits.setting: Surgical inpatients, Lincoln County Hospital NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Pain managed adequately in 30%; anti-emetics offered to 92%.

audits.intervention: Departmental educational presentation.

cycle2.result: Pain managed adequately in 46%; prophylactic laxatives prescribed in 100% of eligible patients; anti-emetics 82%.

audits.other_findings: Inadequate prescribing habits reported as 30% vs 16% between cycles; staff changeover affected prescribing.
audits.citation: Jodlowski G, Joyce D. 75 Audit of Pain Control in Surgical Inpatients. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae163.202.

audits.title: Reducing pain in patients undergoing cardiac surgery after implementation of a quality improvement postoperative pain treatment program.
audits.standard: Acute pain management algorithm; implementation complete when adherence to 2 of 3 process indicators reached at least 70% over 2 months
audits.setting: 18-bed surgical intensive care unit, University Hospitals of Geneva

cycle1.result: Pain at rest VAS 2.7 +/- 1.4 cm; no pain or often without pain 11%; sleep disturbance 68%.

audits.intervention: Pain management algorithm implemented with training, pocket guidelines, regular audits and feedback.

cycle2.result: Pain at rest VAS 2.2 +/- 1.4 cm (P = .008); no pain or often without pain 37% (P = .005); sleep disturbance 35% (P = .012).

audits.other_findings: No differences at 1 and 6 months postoperatively.
audits.citation: Diby M, Romand JA, Frick S, Heidegger CP, Walder B. Reducing pain in patients undergoing cardiac surgery after implementation of a quality improvement postoperative pain treatment program. J Crit Care. 2008;23(3):359-371. doi:10.1016/j.jcrc.2007.11.005. PMID: 18725042.

audits.title: A sustainable method to reduce postoperative oxycodone discharge prescribing in a metropolitan tertiary referral hospital.
audits.standard: not reported
audits.setting: Four surgical wards, St Vincent's Public Hospital, Sydney (tertiary referral hospital)

cycle1.result: Oxycodone tablets rising by 1.8 tablets/100 surgical admissions per month; 27% of oxycodone prescriptions inappropriate.

audits.intervention: Five sequential interventions; the fifth was audit-feedback plus individual academic detailing.

cycle2.result: Tablets fell by 77 per 100 surgical cases after the fifth intervention, then a monthly fall of 3.2 tablets/100 admissions; inappropriate prescriptions fell to 17% (p = 0.048) and then 10% (p = 0.002) after 3 years.

audits.other_findings: The first four interventions produced no significant change.
audits.citation: Stevens J, Trimboli A, Samios P, Steele N, Welch S, Thompson P, et al.. A sustainable method to reduce postoperative oxycodone discharge prescribing in a metropolitan tertiary referral hospital. Anaesthesia. 2019;74(3):292-299. doi:10.1111/anae.14570. PMID: 30623418.

audits.title: Towards Better Perioperative Pain Management in Mexico: A Study in a Network of Hospitals Using Quality Improvement Methods from PAIN OUT.
audits.standard: PAIN OUT patient-reported outcome quality indicators; primary outcome proportion reporting worst pain ≥6/10
audits.setting: Network of 9 hospitals in Mexico City using PAIN OUT audit and feedback

cycle1.result: Patients receiving information about pain treatment options 44% at baseline.

audits.intervention: Locally adapted teaching and pain management resources (website, journal special issue), teaching for anaesthetists, surgeons, residents and nurses, and patient information

audits.title: The effect of education, assessment and a standardised prescription on postoperative pain management. The value of clinical audit in the establishment of acute pain services.
audits.standard: not reported
audits.setting: 15 hospitals (university, large and small district general hospitals) in England and Wales

cycle1.result: 32% of patients had moderate to severe pain at rest; 37% severe pain on movement; 41% moderate to severe pain on deep inspiration.

audits.intervention: Staff and patient education, formal pain assessment and recording, and a standardised algorithm for intermittent intramuscular opioid prescription.

cycle2.result: Moderate to severe pain at rest fell to 12%; severe pain on movement to 13%; moderate to severe pain on deep inspiration to 22%.

audits.other_findings: Nausea and vomiting fell similarly and postoperative complications fell slightly. Sample size 2738 is the total across both surveys.
audits.citation: Harmer M, Davies KA. The effect of education, assessment and a standardised prescription on postoperative pain management. The value of clinical audit in the establishment of acute pain services. Anaesthesia. 1998;53(5):424-430. doi:10.1046/j.1365-2044.1998.00368.x. PMID: 9659013.

audits.title: Evaluating discharge opioid prescribing practices in elective surgical patients: a retrospective audit from a tertiary surgical and rehabilitation centre.
audits.standard: Contemporary opioid stewardship best-practice recommendations
audits.setting: Tertiary surgical and rehabilitation centre (elective surgical inpatients)

cycle1.result: 47.6% (n = 274) discharged with an opioid, mostly oxycodone IR (54.8%) or tapentadol (41.2%), typically fixed quantities of 10 (52.2%) or 5 (27.4%) tablets; discharge oMEDD median 75 mg (IQR 75-150).

audits.intervention: not reported

cycle2.result: not reported

audits.other_findings: Quantity was often standardised rather than tailored and a minority received an opioid despite no recent inpatient need.
audits.citation: Lee K, Pattullo C, Vujcich E. Evaluating discharge opioid prescribing practices in elective surgical patients: a retrospective audit from a tertiary surgical and rehabilitation centre. Aust Health Rev. 2026;50(4):AH26046. doi:10.1071/ah26046. PMID: 42767656.
